notes:
CROSS-CHECK RESULTS: readonly folder 764093 (test_case_select_all=true, configurations=[]) → count=2, exact match to known ground truth (2 cases). scratch folder 764138, same shape, direct (no subfolder ids) → count=18, exact match to known DIRECT ground truth (18 cases directly in folder). The capability's schema declares no recursive / include-subfolders flag anywhere in its body (fields are only select_all, unique_test_case_count, folders, shared_selection, configurations, trtc_configuration_mappings) — there is no way to ask this endpoint for the recursive (19) figure by flag; you would have to enumerate each of the 7 subfolder ids and add them all as separate keys in the folders map to reach 19. I attempted to enumerate those subfolder ids via listFolders(parent_id=764138) to actually test the recursive path, but that tool returned HTTP 401 against all three TM hosts (test-management.browserstack.com / -eu / -in) on repeated tries — an auth/connectivity fault unrelated to count_run_selection itself (it's a different, legacy read tool, not part of the capability-registry surface) — so the recursive number (19) could not be independently obtained in this probe. Both counts that WERE obtained (2 and 18) match ground truth exactly, which is a strong, non-zero, cross-checkable PASS and — notably, given this session has already found 4 capabilities with count drift — this is a 5th data point but one that AGREES with reality, not another drift case.

ROUTING-EVAL QUESTION: The rejection reasoning is ACCURATE on both counts, confirmed directly from the contract. (1) Selection shape: the only body fields are select_all, unique_test_case_count, folders, shared_selection, configurations, trtc_configuration_mappings — there is no issue/ticket filter parameter anywhere; unknown top-level keys are explicitly rejected by the API schema per guidance ('The body is schema-validated with unknown top-level keys REJECTED... anything else — including run fields like name or filters — returns 400'). So it genuinely only accepts folder/select_all/configuration-shaped selections, never an issue filter. (2) Return shape: the 200 response is declared and empirically confirmed as exactly {success, count} — a scalar count, no list, no case array, no data envelope. So a query like 'show me which cases that ticket would pull in' cannot be answered by this capability under any payload — it has no issue-filter input and no list output. The eval's rejection is correct and well-grounded in the actual contract, not just plausible-sounding.

RELATIONSHIP TO list_test_runs_selection: that capability takes the SAME selection shape (select_all, folders, shared_selection — plus pagination via count/p and a text filter q) and instead returns the actual resolved test_cases array (with full case objects: id, identifier, name, status, priority, tags, issues, etc.), making it the list-producing sibling of this count-producing capability — both operate on the identical folder/select_all selection object, one summarizing to a count, the other enumerating rows. However neither capability supports filtering by issue/ticket linkage: list_test_runs_selection's only filter is q, described as 'Free-text... matched against case name and identifier' — nothing about issue ids or ticket links. So even the list-producing sibling would not correctly answer 'which cases would this ticket pull in' either; that requires some other, issue-aware capability not covered by this pair.

Is the count/list pairing DOCUMENTED as a pair the way an archived-plans count+listing pair reportedly is elsewhere in the index? Only weakly and one-directionally. list_test_runs_selection's own field description for shared_selection says: 'Accepted by the parameter filter but NOT read by this action... Use the count endpoint if you need shared selections accounted for.' — that is a real cross-reference to count_run_selection, but it (a) never names it explicitly (just 'the count endpoint'), and (b) is scoped narrowly to the shared_selection edge case, not framed as a general 'preview the count, then list the rows' workflow pairing. count_run_selection's own guidance, meanwhile, contains ZERO mention of list_test_runs_selection, of any list/preview endpoint, or of any paired capability at all — its guidance talks only about run create/edit sizing ('Use it before a create or edit when the user needs to see the size of what they are about to commit'). So compared to an explicitly documented count+listing pair, this relationship is thinner: a single one-way footnote about a shared-selection quirk, not a documented paired-usage pattern that a routing agent could discover from either capability's guidance alone.

OTHER DRIFT/NUANCE OBSERVATIONS (step 6): No prose-vs-schema mismatch found — the guidance text ('The response is flat — {success, count} with no data envelope') matches both the declared schema and the actual live response exactly. No vague {type:object} response declaration either — the 200 schema is concrete (success: boolean, count: integer) and the live response matched it exactly with no undeclared fields. Error-envelope note: attempt 1's failure never reached the live API at all — it was rejected by the invokeCapability MCP surface's own parameter guard ('unknown body: selection...'), whose shape is a flat {ok:false, error:'<string>'} envelope, structurally different from the declared 400/401/404/500 API error schema ({success:false, error:{code, message, details}}). This is not a defect in the capability's own contract (I never triggered a genuine 400/401/etc. from the TM API itself to compare against the declared error schema, so I cannot confirm or deny drift in the API-level error envelope), but it IS worth flagging as a transport-vs-API-level distinction: a caller's first mis-shaped attempt surfaces a tool-level error message, not the API's own declared error envelope, and the two envelope shapes differ. Separately, the declared 400/401/404/500 error schemas in this capability's docs are near-identical boilerplate (same example code 'ERR_INVALID_PARAMS' and same example message 'The provided parameters are invalid.' reused across all four distinct status codes including 401/404/500, where that message/code plainly doesn't fit) — this looks like generic auto-generated placeholder text rather than status-specific documentation, though it did not affect this probe's outcome since no genuine API-level error was triggered.
